the gas in its cylinders—now numbering
eight—to generate energy.
dex.967:
It can sprint at over 70 mph while
carrying a human. The rider's body
heat warms Cyclizar's back and lifts
the Pokémon's spirit.
dex.968:
This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It
maintains its metal body by consuming
iron from the soil.
dex.969:
Glimmet's toxic mineral crystals look
just like flower petals. This Pokémon
scatters poisonous powder like pollen
to protect itself.
dex.970:
Glimmora's petals are made of
crystallized poison energy. It has
recently become evident that these
petals resemble Tera Jewels.
dex.971:
This friendly Pokémon doesn't like
being alone. Pay it even the slightest
bit of attention, and it will follow
you forever.
dex.972:
A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn
as Houndstone. It doesn't like anyone
touching the protuberance atop its
head.
dex.973:
This Pokémon apparently ties the base
of its neck into a knot so that energy
stored in its belly does not escape
from its beak.
dex.974:
It lives in frigid regions in pods of
five or so individuals. It loves the
minerals found in snow and ice.
dex.975:
Ice energy builds up in the horn on
its upper jaw, causing the horn to
reach cryogenic temperatures that
freeze its surroundings.
dex.976:
Veluza has excellent regenerative
capabilities. It sheds spare flesh
from its body to boost its agility,
then charges at its prey.
dex.977:
It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and
follows it loyally. Though powerful,
Dondozo is apparently not very smart.
dex.978:
Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning
Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in
prey, then orders its partner to
attack.
dex.979:
When its anger rose beyond a critical
point, this Pokémon gained power that
is unfettered by the limits of its
physical body.
dex.980:
It lives at the bottom of ponds and
swamps. It will carry Wooper on its
back and ferry them across water from
one shore to the other.
dex.981:
The hardened head from the tail
protects the head of the main body as
Farigiraf whips its long neck around
to headbutt enemies.
dex.982:
It drives enemies out of its nest by
sucking in enough air to fill its
long, narrow lungs, then releasing the
air in an intense blast.
dex.983:
Though it commands a massive army in
battle, it's not skilled at devising
complex strategies. It just uses brute
strength to keep pushing.
dex.984:
This creature resembles a mysterious
Pokémon that, according to a
paranormal magazine, has lived since
ancient times.
dex.985:
It resembles a mysterious Pokémon
described in a paranormal magazine as
a Jigglypuff from one billion years
ago.
dex.986:
It bears a slight resemblance to a
Pokémon described in a dubious
magazine as a cross between a dinosaur
and a mushroom.
dex.987:
It has similar features to a ghostly
pterosaur that was covered in a
paranormal magazine, but the two have
little else in common.
dex.988:
This Pokémon somewhat resembles an
ancient form of Volcarona that was
introduced in a dubious magazine.
dex.989:
It slightly resembles a Magneton that
lived for 10,000 years and was
featured in an article in a paranormal
magazine.
dex.990:
Sightings of this Pokémon have
occurred in recent years. It resembles
a mysterious object described in an
old expedition journal.
dex.991:

mentioned in an old book. There are
only two reported sightings of this
Pokémon.
dex.992:
This Pokémon shares many similarities
with Iron Hands, an object mentioned
in a certain expedition journal.
dex.993:
It's possible that Iron Jugulis, an
object described in an old book, may
actually be this Pokémon.
dex.994:
No records exist of this species being
caught. Data is lacking, but the
Pokémon's traits match up with an
object described in an old book.
dex.995:
Some of its notable features match
those of an object named within a
certain expedition journal as Iron
Thorns.
dex.996:
This Pokémon lives in forests and
craggy areas. Using the power of its
dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its
nest like a refrigerator.
dex.997:
Arctibax freezes the air around it,
protecting its face with an ice mask
and turning its dorsal fin into a
blade of ice.
dex.998:
It launches itself into battle by
flipping upside down and spewing
frigid air from its mouth. It finishes
opponents off with its dorsal blade.
dex.999:
It lives inside an old treasure chest.
Sometimes it gets left in shop corners
since no one realizes it's actually a
Pokémon.
